mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals increased demand for housing and related goods, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which can lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (growth < 0.3% in the same period), it signals strong economic growth without significant inflation, which is conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows > 2% QoQ & CPIAUCSL grows < 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
